audit_findings.title: Declared post-year dividend is absent from the dated bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $23.387m computed from $2.00 times 11,693,481 shares outstanding on August 13, 2026; approximately $1.96 per valuation share and 2.9% of base equity value
audit_findings.evidence: On July 15, 2026 , our Board of Directors declared a special cash dividend of $ 1.05 per share and a regular annual cash dividend of $ 0.95 per share on all issued and outstanding shares of Common Stock and Class A Stock of the Company (the “August 2026 Dividends”).
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated dated-bridge omission unless the valuation explicitly includes the detached dividend receivable. By September 6 the dividend belonged to August 17 record holders, while the June 25 cash balance had not been reduced for the September 9 payment. Deducting approximately $1.96 per valuation share would reduce the reported base value from $68.14 to about $66.18 and bull value from $76.10 to about $74.14.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether a September 6 purchaser receives the dividend. If not, rerun all scenarios with a $23.387m dividend-payable deduction, updated for the exact August 17 eligible share count if available.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded SERP claim may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $29.952m gross projected benefit obligation; $22.464m after the filed $7.488m retirement-plan deferred tax asset, approximately $1.88 per valuation share and 2.8% of base equity value
audit_findings.evidence: The Supplemental Employee Retirement Plan (“SERP”) is an unfunded, non-qualified benefit plan that will provide eligible participants with monthly benefits upon retirement, disability or death, subject to certain conditions.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed SERP obligation is demonstrated and the bridge shows no separate deduction. Pension expense in earnings does not by itself prove that owner earnings captures cash benefit payments or runoff of the existing obligation. The remaining uncertainty is whether the OE calculation already substitutes benefit payments for pension expense; absent that adjustment, the net unfunded claim is material and the bridge overstates equity value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile OE to the $2.118m fiscal-2026 pension cost, $0.534m benefits paid, $29.952m obligation, $29.952m recognized current and noncurrent liabilities, and $7.488m deferred tax asset; then deduct the net claim or rerun OE using benefit-payment cash flows without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest violates the premise that interest remains inside OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.780m fiscal-2026 capitalized interest, equal to 2.9% of the $61.1m anchor OE; post-disbursement forecast effect unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: The interest capitalized in fiscal 2026 was $ 1,780 .
audit_findings.explanation: It is demonstrated that fiscal-2026 GAAP earnings excluded $1.780m of equipment-loan interest, but the record does not show whether the OE calculation manually deducted it or captured it through maintenance capital expenditure. The loan's final rate and full fiscal-2027 interest burden are also unavailable, so the continuing valuation effect cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the FY2026 OE reconciliation for a capitalized-interest or corresponding capital-expenditure deduction, obtain the final equipment-loan disbursement and fixed-rate schedule, and rerun forecast OE for the actual interest and amortization period if missing.

audit_findings.title: Signed Huntley lease introduces recurring cost absent from the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $17.943m filed additional operating-lease commitment, equal to 2.2% of $813m base equity value or $1.50 per valuation share; annual OE expense unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: Since the lease for the remaining space has not yet commenced, approximately $ 17,943 of additional operating leases are not reflected in the Consolidated Balance Sheet and tables above.
audit_findings.explanation: The signed ten-year commitment is demonstrated and begins in fiscal 2027, so its recurring expense is absent from the FY2026 anchor. Its filed commitment is large enough to affect the narrow spread between market price and bull value, but the correct adjustment is the incremental annual occupancy expense in forecast OE, not automatically a second deduction of the entire lease amount.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the Huntley payment schedule, commencement date, straight-line lease expense, variable property-tax, insurance and operating costs, and any offsetting savings; rerun each scenario with the net incremental cost in every applicable forecast year.

audit_findings.title: Known fiscal-2027 completion spending may exceed modeled reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $48.0m filed fiscal-2027 capital-expenditure forecast, equal to 78.6% of anchor OE and 5.9% of base equity value; unmodeled portion unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: We expect total capital expenditures for equipment purchases and upgrades for fiscal 2027 to be approximately $48.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The spending forecast is demonstrated, but the record does not allocate it among maintenance already reflected in normalized OE, committed project completion, and discretionary expansion. Nor does it show the dollar reinvestment generated by the 13.7% RONTA calculation. Consequently, the existence and materiality of any double count or omission cannot yet be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $48.0m project-by-project to normalized maintenance capex and each scenario's explicit RONTA reinvestment charge, then rerun fiscal 2027 and later cash flows for any committed spending not captured while retaining only growth supported by that spending.

audit_findings.title: Customer concentration permits a level break below the zero-growth bear case
audit_findings.magnitude: 53% of fiscal-2026 net sales, approximately $623.1m computed from $1,175.673m; Walmart approximately 41% or $482.0m and Target approximately 12% or $141.1m; OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: In total, sales to these two customers represented approximately 53 % , 51 % and 52 % of our net sales in fiscal 2026, fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The concentration is filed, but no customer loss, adverse award decision or permanent repricing is demonstrated. It is therefore a forward-looking level-break risk rather than a current numerical error. Because every scenario preserves at least the $61.1m OE level, an actual major-customer loss could make even the zero-growth bear case too high.
audit_findings.action: Monitor post-year bidding outcomes, awards, discontinuations, pricing concessions and committed volumes. If adverse evidence emerges, estimate the affected contribution profit and stranded fixed costs and rerun a lower normalized anchor or explicit negative-growth downside case.
